#### What this PR does / why we need it:

1. Updates `kube-openapi` and `gengo` to pull in new declarative defaults feature
2. Adds a script to compare defaulting from OpenAPI `spec.Schema` to handwritten defaults using `runtime.Scheme`
3. Populates missing defaults where possible (some things we cannot do like defaults of arrays with constants, or custom defaults for each usage of pod template)

I might have missed that but,
1. How do you know which values you need to default?
2. How do you make sure you're not changing the existing behavior?

> How do you know which values you need to default?

The new tool added to the repo compares the native and schema-based defaults and outputs markdown seen in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119766. I've just been going through that list and populating anything the existing native defaults do that the schema does not. There are no existing cases of the schema populating a default that handwritten does not

> How do you make sure you're not changing the existing behavior?

We have defaults unit tests to ensure defaults are populated for the existing native tests. It is hard to know for sure because a code coverage analysis wouldn't necessarily guarantee we are actually checking the default value, just that it was populated. We could go through by hand to ensure there is a test for each case. That would not be completely impractical since there are not that many missing defaults.
